objective: Stop coverage_report from reporting a fault as SIMULATED on the strength of its name: require an execution record naming the injector, an injected or observed outcome, and a reference to the output.
decision_supported: Is a caller-provided list of fault names evidence of simulated coverage, or does the report need the injector execution behind each claim?
acceptance: coverage_report() with no evidence reports every fault NOT_EXECUTED.
A simulated claim without an execution record is refused.
A skipped or failed outcome is refused rather than counted as coverage.
A record without an evidence_ref or without an injector name is refused.
Evidence supplied for a fault that is not claimed grants nothing.
Each SIMULATED entry carries its evidence reference in the report.
HARDWARE_TESTED still requires a named physical evidence reference.
The report stays JSON-serializable and versioned.
evidence: Before the change, coverage_report(simulated=declared_faults()) reported all eight faults SIMULATED without running any injector.
After the change the same call is refused with 'claims SIMULATED without an execution record'.
With a record naming an injector, an observed outcome and an evidence_ref, the fault is SIMULATED and the report carries simulation_evidence_ref.
A skipped or failed outcome, a blank reference and a blank injector are each refused with their own message.
stop_conditions: An existing injector test cannot produce an evidence reference; the reference is a path the test already knows, so this is not expected.
risks_and_fallbacks: Callers that passed only names now fail loudly; the two tests in the repository were the only callers and both were updated.
The record is validated for shape and outcome, not for the content of the referenced file; hashing the artifact is a separate change.
